changes.after: Split puts values with the same group label together, so each group can have its own average.

before: split(values, groups) returns a list of vectors, one per grouping level. Here a contains 2 and NA while b contains 6. Equal-length input and group vectors avoid unintended recycling; missing group labels need an explicit policy.

mean averages a numeric vector. na.rm = TRUE removes missing observations for each group; an all-missing group can produce NaN rather than an informative average. Removing missing observations changes which data support each estimate, so record counts as well when needed.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
values <- c(2, NA, 6)
groups <- c("a", "a", "b")
parts <- split(values, groups)
result <- vapply(parts, function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
cat(result, "\n")
```
Expected output or behavior: 2 6. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Compute each group's mean using its known values.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```r
values <- c(2, NA, 6)
groups <- c("a", "a", "b")
parts <- split(values, groups)
result <- vapply(parts, function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
cat(result, "\n")
```
The output is `2 6`. Group a has just two left after skipping the missing entry. Group b has six.
Keep the missing entry in the average for group a.
